approach.method_basis: The Parent alternates direct molecular sampling from a task-local neural flow policy with two rounds of graph crossover and mutation. It learns from the exact token trajectories and real scores of accepted molecules through trajectory balance, a jointly learned normalizer and regularization toward a frozen corpus-trained prior. Accepted graph discoveries re-enter the same replay archive. A fingerprint Gaussian posterior selects which fresh graph offspring receive evaluations while retaining the first fresh-policy handoff. Its reusable prior is chosen along the unchanged unlabeled training trajectory by fixed-noise valid, connected, unique molecular yield, with original holdout loss breaking ties. Online replay currently samples the full accepted archive by global score rank.
approach.novelty: Add a scaffold-balanced mixture to accepted trajectory replay: keep half of each trajectory's original rank probability and allocate the other half equally among available core families, preserving rank preference within each family. This changes which genuine accepted trajectories train the policy, with every accepted label and exact serialization retained. The lineage's other children changed prior preparation or graph posterior selection; none changed replay allocation. Other campaign experiments balanced breeding parents or survivor populations and lost score despite broader core use. This experiment tests a different path, the distribution of neural learning credit over the full accepted archive, and explicitly checks later policy behavior rather than treating extra scaffold counts as success.

hypothesis: Sample accepted trajectory-balance replay from an equal mixture of inherited score-rank probabilities and uniform scaffold-group mass with the inherited conditional rank probabilities preserved within each group.

finding_summary.headline: Scaffold-balanced replay broadened learning exposure and reached the policy, while completed-seed endpoints worsened
finding_summary.insights: Extra archive coverage did reach neural learning and subsequent sampling, so the result rules out a purely cosmetic entropy increase. It also exposes the allocation tradeoff: on the same accepted histories the mixture cuts expected graph-origin mass from 72.53% to 59.12% and reduces high-score rank emphasis, while giving much more replay to lower-ranked policy and initial records. Some transfer measures and average policy scores improve, yet those changes coexist with fewer novel raw candidates and weaker completed-seed best results. Broad replay therefore does not establish better endpoint search. The chemical assessment reinforces the distinction: plausible cyclic amines coexist with peroxide, N-halogen and constrained unsaturated-ring families, so family breadth does not certify useful functional context. The terminal failure is a separate inherited canonicalization weakness exposed by one emitted molecule; it explains the missing third formal score and does not explain the losses in the two successful seeds. A complete three-seed score-benefit conclusion remains unavailable.
finding_summary.results: The declared replay mixture ran in all 449 executed feedback states. Actual distinct scaffold groups per 32-member update rose from 17.87 to 23.26, with broader exposure in all fifteen task sessions. Graph-origin replay received less probability, but its average sampled trajectory log-probability increase rose slightly from 0.169 to 0.176 nats and more later policy emissions occupied previously trained graph families. Mean accepted policy-origin score increased from 0.205 to 0.238. This did not improve every output measure: raw valid-novel yield fell from 66.59% to 64.74%, duplicates increased, and emitted scaffold coverage narrowed slightly. Both formally successful seed endpoints fell, by 0.02618 and 0.06224. The third seed completed its oracle calls but failed on the final canonical-identity feedback join, leaving its formal macro score unavailable.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich output mixes plausible cyclic amines with peroxides, N-halogen bonds and severely constrained unsaturated rings
molecular.overall_character: All five supplied tasks cover all three seeds, with 900 trajectory rows and 870 optimizer proposals per task. All 4,350 optimizer proposals parse with RDKit, but their chemical plausibility varies substantially. The output is rich in rings and aromatic atoms: digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9782 to 0.9954 and aromatic-token rates from 0.9103 to 0.9759. Median proposal heavy-atom counts are 26, 35, 26, 32 and 25 in the fixed task order, with median ring counts of three, five, four, four and three. Conventional diaryl ethers, thioamides, aryl sulfonamides, heteroaromatic carbonyl systems, cyclic tertiary amines and arylpiperazines coexist with diaryl peroxides, N-chloro or N-fluoro groups, densely fused sulfur/nitrogen frameworks and small rings bearing cumulated carbon double bonds. Each task contains 529-717 distinct nonchiral Murcko scaffolds, but many digest leaders are variants within a few families; graph-level diversity does not establish accessible synthetic diversity. Relative to the parent, one leading repertoire becomes enriched in peroxides, another in small-ring allenes and N-halogen bonds, while the strongest cyclic-amine chemistry includes smaller, recognizable benzazepine-like structures. No assigned stereocentres occur among optimizer proposals, despite 273, 179, 562, 373 and 348 proposals containing an unassigned centre in task order. Synthetic plausibility is therefore questionable overall, with clear plausible subsets; the supplied scores do not establish stability, synthetic access or experimental activity.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family contains two methyl-substituted phenyl rings connected by an ether or peroxide, with an aryl thioamide attached to a diazine ring. The ether has 24 heavy atoms and the peroxide 25; both have three aromatic six-membered rings. Other leaders are compact fused azaaromatic ketones and a fused aromatic carbonyl/N-N heterocycle. Those carbonyl and thioamide frameworks are recognizable chemistry, but the peroxide, N-chloro amide/thioamide and unusual sulfur double-bond variants make part of the leading family chemically questionable as persistent drug-like molecules. The whole proposal set has median 26 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings. Compared with the parent, O-O single-bond proposals increase from 15 to 89 and N-halogen proposals from five to 27, so the new leading peroxide chemistry reflects a broader change in the sampled output.
liabilities: Diaryl O-O links and N-chloro or N-fluoro nitrogen sites introduce possible bond-cleavage and reactivity concerns; valid SMILES and objective values do not resolve those concerns.

The terminal sulfur-linked N-fluoro example and sulfur oxo/thioxo substitutions are chemically different from ordinary amides or sulfonamides and should not be interpreted as interchangeable polar linkers.
Nine proposals have at most three heavy atoms and four exceed 50, indicating occasional degeneration and overgrowth around an otherwise ring-rich population.
missing_features: The high-score neighborhood lacks demonstrated stable, conventional alternatives that retain the useful diaryl/polar arrangement while replacing its peroxide and N-halogen variants; the high-scoring ether shows such chemistry is already reachable.
Broader coverage of distinct compact aromatic carbonyl arrangements is less visible among the digest leaders than repeated changes around the same diaryl linker and thioamide family.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Replacing the diaryl ether link with an O-O link accompanies a score increase from 0.444319 to 0.455132 in a displayed local pair. Adding N-chlorination to the peroxide thioamide gives 0.439920, and the corresponding N-chloro carbonyl amide gives 0.438748. These observations show that the score tolerates the questionable bonds; they do not establish a benefit from N-chlorination or the chemical stability of a peroxide. Compact fused aromatic carbonyl structures also reach 0.436954 and 0.433013 without those particular bonds. At the low end, oxygen fluoride, methane and trifluoromethylamine score zero, while much larger, heavily elaborated molecules score about 1.05e-68 and 1.11e-62. The gradient therefore favors a structured intermediate-size aromatic/polar arrangement over both tiny fragments and overgrowth, while leaving some local chemical liabilities unpenalized.

per_task.generated_character: This is a large, highly aromatic, halogenated repertoire: median 35 heavy atoms, five rings, four aromatic rings and molecular mass 555.2495; the digest halogen rate is 0.8241. The highest molecule is a comparatively conventional three-ring aminoheteroaryl arylsulfonamide with methyl, fluoromethyl and aryl halogen substituents. Other leaders combine nitrogen/sulfur heteroaromatics with sulfonyl groups, carbonyls and heavily fused, iodine- or bromine-substituted ring systems. One displayed leader has eight rings and seven aromatic rings, and a terminal example contains selenium. The parent also contained large heteroaryl/sulfur frameworks and frequent peroxide or O-halogen connections. Current O-O single-bond proposals fall from 135 to five and O-halogen proposals from 93 to four, but substantial size and fusion remain: 146 current proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms.
liabilities: Large aromatic surfaces, iodine or bromine substitution and repeated ring fusion produce high molecular masses and little saturated shape in many leaders; no solubility or exposure measurements are supplied.

Some terminal molecules combine unusual nitrogen/oxygen/sulfur bonding or selenium heterocycles with already elaborate fused systems, increasing the uncertainty of interpreting them as ordinary medicinal chemistry.
The proposal distribution reaches 95 heavy atoms and 13 perceived rings; such overgrowth is not justified by the simpler structure at the highest displayed score.
missing_features: The output lacks consistent economical coverage of the productive aminoheteroaryl/sulfonamide arrangement: the highest displayed molecule is much simpler than several heavily fused alternatives.
Synthetic access and stable geometry are not established for the densely fused sulfur/nitrogen leaders; graph ring counts cannot substitute for chemically credible alternative ring systems.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The three-ring aminoheteroaryl sulfonamide scores 0.607553; a six-ring iodine-containing fused system scores 0.604646 and an eight-ring elaboration 0.598471. These examples do not support continually adding rings or heavy halogens as necessary for higher score. The low-scoring examples, around 0.265-0.292, also contain sulfones, carbonyls and sometimes several rings, but distribute them through more saturated or differently connected frameworks. Functional-group presence alone therefore fails to explain the gradient. A terminal small fluorinated diene scores 0.5 despite lacking the elaborate heteroaromatic architecture, so intermediate score itself is weak evidence of molecular completeness.

per_task.generated_character: The leading chemistry is substantially more conventional than the most unusual output elsewhere. The highest displayed molecule is a phenolic benzazepine-like structure: a seven-membered tertiary-amine ring fused to a benzene, with alkyl substituents, only 18 heavy atoms and molecular mass 247.382. A closely related leader has 17 heavy atoms. Another family is an arylpiperazine linked through a long alkyl chain to fluorinated naphthalene or aza-naphthalene rings; these examples have four rings and approximately 29-32 heavy atoms. The full set has median 26 heavy atoms and median sp3-carbon fraction 0.5. Parent leaders also included arylpiperazine chains and fused phenolic amines, but some were much more bridged or polycyclic; current median heavy-atom count falls from 30 to 26.
liabilities: Long alkyl chains in the arylpiperazine family increase conformational freedom, and extra halogenation increases mass, while the compact phenolic amine shows that neither feature is universally needed.
Some terminal structures add strained or partially dearomatized rings and duplicated arylpiperazine appendages; these are less straightforward chemical proposals than the leading conventional amines.
Thirty proposals contain an N-halogen bond, but the displayed highest-scoring conventional amines do not require that liability.
missing_features: No additional mandatory pharmacophoric group can be inferred from near-ceiling scores; the supported missing chemistry is configurationally specified coverage of the successful cyclic amines.

The compact leading phenolic amines have an unassigned stereogenic carbon. Across proposals, 562 molecules contain an unassigned centre and none has an assigned centre, leaving geometry-dependent interpretation unresolved.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Both the compact phenolic cyclic amine and the long-linker arylpiperazines reach scores above 0.999999. Their shared association is accessible tertiary-amine functionality presented with aromatic regions; extensive halogenation, multiple aromatic rings or one exact linker length is not required by all leading examples. An acetylated bis-sulfonamide aniline scores about 3.80e-05 and an aromatic carbamate about 9.56e-05, despite their heteroatoms and rings. The terminal shorter fluoroalkyl diazepane scores 0.036190, whereas related extended arylpiperazine architectures remain around 0.975-0.996. These observations indicate contextual amine/aromatic placement rather than generic nitrogen enrichment, and do not establish experimental receptor activity.

per_task.generated_character: The leading repertoire is dominated by fused azaaromatic systems with N-methylated cyclic amide carbonyls, supplemented by a bicyclic amine/ketone family carrying an N-ethoxy connection and an aromatic ether arm. The highest molecule has 30 heavy atoms, five rings and four aromatic rings; closely related N-alkyl variants occupy much of the digest. Several carbonyl-bearing rings are seven- or eight-membered within multiply fused frameworks, and another leader has a perceived nine-membered ring. These are complex rather than sparse ring systems. Full proposals have median 32 heavy atoms and four rings, with 668 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds. Parent leaders also included N-methyl cyclic carbonyl systems and aromatic assemblies, with additional sulfonylpiperazine chemistry; the current digest is more visibly concentrated in fused carbonyl/N-alkyl variants.
liabilities: Complex fused and bridged carbonyl frameworks may impose synthetic and conformational constraints that their accepted SMILES do not capture.
N-O bonds in the N-ethoxy family and unusual N/N/O ring arrangements deserve separate chemical scrutiny; their presence is not interchangeable with a conventional ether or amine.
Sixty proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, and 373 contain an unassigned stereocentre, so size and geometry remain unresolved even though rings and carbonyls are plentiful.
missing_features: The leading set lacks broad chemically distinct alternatives that preserve the observed aromatic and cyclic-carbonyl arrangement; much of the visible variation changes N-alkyl groups or local ring closure.
No supplied evidence establishes stable conformations or accessible syntheses for the unusual fusion patterns, and the N-ethoxy bicyclic leader leaves a stereocentre unspecified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fused N-aryl carbonyl framework reaches 0.202215, the N-ethoxy bicyclic amine/ketone example 0.200010, and several nearby fused N-alkyl variants approximately 0.197-0.199. These small differences do not identify a unique missing substituent. The low end includes oxygen bonded to fluorine and chlorine at zero, bromopropane at 0.018950, ethyl acetate at 0.030544 and a small amino heterocycle at 0.041345. Those lack the combined aromatic/cyclic-carbonyl architecture of the leaders. A long-chain sulfur-rich cyclic molecule also scores only 0.031469, demonstrating that molecular size and heteroatom abundance alone are insufficient. Late, related N/O-rich fused carbonyl structures remain around 0.16-0.18 rather than establishing a different high-score chemotype.

per_task.generated_character: The highest family combines a fused nitrogen-rich dicarbonyl heterocycle, N-methyl and N-fluoro substituents, a hydroxylated azaaryl ring and a four-membered carbon ring. In the two highest displayed molecules that small ring contains a cumulated C=C=C unit; another leader contains a four-membered conjugated diene. These are severe ring-geometry liabilities, despite all SMILES parsing. Other leading families contain an N-acetyl arylsulfonamide with a sulfinamide substituent and unsaturated fluorinated five-membered rings, or hydrazone/polyene chains ending in a charged nitrogen/oxygen/sulfur group. Median proposal size is 25 heavy atoms and three rings. Compared with the parent, N-halogen proposals rise from five to 157, carbon-allene proposals from one to 113, and proposals with a carbon allene contained in a perceived ring of at most five atoms from zero to 93. The current chemistry is therefore not simply a conventional heteroaromatic analogue series.
liabilities: There are 93 proposals with a carbon allene in a perceived ring of at most five atoms, and 62 with a four-membered ring containing at least two double bonds. Their constrained unsaturation is a chemical-realizability concern that ordinary valence parsing does not test.

N-halogen bonds occur in 157 proposals, and the digest charged rate is 0.2471; the leading N-F and unusual charged sulfur/nitrogen forms require stronger chemical qualification than neutral carbonyl heterocycles.
Twenty-five proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, while repeated small-ring or heterocycle duplication can produce vanishing scores without removing the original local liabilities.
missing_features: The leading neighborhood lacks demonstrated ordinary, geometrically credible ring alternatives preserving the useful carbonyl/azaaryl arrangement without a four-membered allene or diene.

Stable nitrogen substitution and sulfur/nitrogen electronic structures are not established for the N-fluoro and charged terminal-group families; the observed scores do not establish that these unusual bonds are required.
Configurationally explicit proposals are absent despite 348 molecules having an unassigned centre; the highest small-ring-allene examples also leave a stereogenic centre unspecified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-fluoro dicarbonyl structures with a four-membered cyclic allene score 0.419765; the related four-membered diene scores 0.401915. A fluorinated five-membered diene sulfonamide scores 0.369632 and its cyclic-allene counterpart 0.366311. These values associate compact polar heterocycles and unsaturated substituent arrangements with higher score, but cannot establish stable realizable chemistry or a general benefit from cumulated bonds. The digest median is 0.001873, while eleven full-trajectory rows are exactly zero. Very large linked structures and long-chain polyamines populate that zero-score tail; duplicating the unusual N-halogen dicarbonyl framework in a terminal molecule gives approximately 1.63e-26. Compactness helps explain part of the visible gradient, while serious local bonding liabilities remain in the leaders.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A diaryl peroxide scores 0.455132 while the corresponding ether scores 0.444319, and N-chlorinated derivatives remain nearby. Another session has 157 N-halogen proposals, 113 carbon-allene proposals and 93 with an allene inside a perceived ring of at most five atoms; its highest structures carry both N-F and four-membered cumulated unsaturation. All proposals parse with RDKit, so these liabilities survive ordinary molecular-graph acceptance. Conventional aromatic carbonyl and cyclic-amine leaders elsewhere show that unusual bonds are not universally needed for appreciable reward.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve ordinary bond chemistry and feasible ring geometry within productive structural neighborhoods.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The missing capability is reliable access to stable, geometrically credible alternatives that retain a useful arrangement of rings and polar groups. Chemical plausibility needs to distinguish ethers from peroxides, ordinary N-substitution from N-halogen bonds, and accessible unsaturated rings from extremely constrained cumulenes, independently of objective identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Median heavy-atom counts are 26, 35, 26, 32 and 25, but 4, 146, 7, 60 and 25 proposals respectively exceed 50 heavy atoms. Tiny fragments such as oxygen-halogen species or simple esters also occur at the low end. In one session the highest displayed aminoheteroaryl sulfonamide has three rings, whereas six- and eight-ring alternatives have slightly lower scores. In another, a phenolic tertiary amine with 18 heavy atoms reaches near-ceiling score alongside much larger arylpiperazines. Duplicating a polar heterocycle can coincide with a score around 1.63e-26.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has inconsistent control of molecular size and topology around otherwise useful chemical arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Useful chemical coverage requires economical alternatives with controlled ring fusion, linker length and appendage size, while retaining demonstrated compact and extended chemotypes. A fixed preference for either very small molecules or maximal ring growth would miss the contextual structural relationships visible in the supplied feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across 4,350 optimizer proposals there are no assigned stereocentres. The five supplied sessions contain 273, 179, 562, 373 and 348 proposals with an unassigned centre. Digest leaders include a compact phenolic cyclic amine, an N-ethoxy bicyclic amine/ketone and fluorinated unsaturated rings with unspecified configurations. Ring richness therefore does not imply defined three-dimensional molecular proposals.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits stereogenic structures without specifying their configurations or resolving relevant bond geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The chemical representation needs to support explicit, internally consistent stereoisomers and bond geometries wherever those degrees of freedom exist. Their usefulness must remain determined by observed feedback, without assuming an unobserved preferred configuration or requiring stereochemistry in naturally achiral chemotypes.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Each session contains 529-717 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds, yet the displayed leaders repeatedly vary diaryl thioamide linkers, fused sulfonyl heterocycles, arylpiperazine chains, N-alkyl cyclic-carbonyl systems or N-fluoro dicarbonyl cores. Several nearby variants have identical or very similar scores. The leaders also demonstrate that nitrogen environments are not interchangeable: conventional tertiary amines, acylated nitrogens, sulfonamide nitrogens and N-halogen forms occupy very different chemical contexts.
transferable_gaps.gap: Many graph scaffolds do not translate into broad coverage of chemically distinct productive core arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs chemically meaningful alternatives in core connectivity and polar-group placement, beyond peripheral halogen changes, N-alkyl substitutions and new ring closures. Preserve the ability to explore different stable architectures that realize an observed useful arrangement, while distinguishing functional-group electronic context and avoiding any prescribed objective-specific scaffold.

method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

finding_summary.headline: Scaffold-balanced replay broadened learning exposure and reached the policy, while completed-seed endpoints worsened
finding_summary.insights: Extra archive coverage did reach neural learning and subsequent sampling, so the result rules out a purely cosmetic entropy increase. It also exposes the allocation tradeoff: on the same accepted histories the mixture cuts expected graph-origin mass from 72.53% to 59.12% and reduces high-score rank emphasis, while giving much more replay to lower-ranked policy and initial records. Some transfer measures and average policy scores improve, yet those changes coexist with fewer novel raw candidates and weaker completed-seed best results. Broad replay therefore does not establish better endpoint search. The chemical assessment reinforces the distinction: plausible cyclic amines coexist with peroxide, N-halogen and constrained unsaturated-ring families, so family breadth does not certify useful functional context. The terminal failure is a separate inherited canonicalization weakness exposed by one emitted molecule; it explains the missing third formal score and does not explain the losses in the two successful seeds. A complete three-seed score-benefit conclusion remains unavailable.
finding_summary.results: The declared replay mixture ran in all 449 executed feedback states. Actual distinct scaffold groups per 32-member update rose from 17.87 to 23.26, with broader exposure in all fifteen task sessions. Graph-origin replay received less probability, but its average sampled trajectory log-probability increase rose slightly from 0.169 to 0.176 nats and more later policy emissions occupied previously trained graph families. Mean accepted policy-origin score increased from 0.205 to 0.238. This did not improve every output measure: raw valid-novel yield fell from 66.59% to 64.74%, duplicates increased, and emitted scaffold coverage narrowed slightly. Both formally successful seed endpoints fell, by 0.02618 and 0.06224. The third seed completed its oracle calls but failed on the final canonical-identity feedback join, leaving its formal macro score unavailable.

molecular_assessment.headline: Ring-rich output mixes plausible cyclic amines with peroxides, N-halogen bonds and severely constrained unsaturated rings
molecular_assessment.overall_character: All five supplied tasks cover all three seeds, with 900 trajectory rows and 870 optimizer proposals per task. All 4,350 optimizer proposals parse with RDKit, but their chemical plausibility varies substantially. The output is rich in rings and aromatic atoms: digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9782 to 0.9954 and aromatic-token rates from 0.9103 to 0.9759. Median proposal heavy-atom counts are 26, 35, 26, 32 and 25 in the fixed task order, with median ring counts of three, five, four, four and three. Conventional diaryl ethers, thioamides, aryl sulfonamides, heteroaromatic carbonyl systems, cyclic tertiary amines and arylpiperazines coexist with diaryl peroxides, N-chloro or N-fluoro groups, densely fused sulfur/nitrogen frameworks and small rings bearing cumulated carbon double bonds. Each task contains 529-717 distinct nonchiral Murcko scaffolds, but many digest leaders are variants within a few families; graph-level diversity does not establish accessible synthetic diversity. Relative to the parent, one leading repertoire becomes enriched in peroxides, another in small-ring allenes and N-halogen bonds, while the strongest cyclic-amine chemistry includes smaller, recognizable benzazepine-like structures. No assigned stereocentres occur among optimizer proposals, despite 273, 179, 562, 373 and 348 proposals containing an unassigned centre in task order. Synthetic plausibility is therefore questionable overall, with clear plausible subsets; the supplied scores do not establish stability, synthetic access or experimental activity.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family contains two methyl-substituted phenyl rings connected by an ether or peroxide, with an aryl thioamide attached to a diazine ring. The ether has 24 heavy atoms and the peroxide 25; both have three aromatic six-membered rings. Other leaders are compact fused azaaromatic ketones and a fused aromatic carbonyl/N-N heterocycle. Those carbonyl and thioamide frameworks are recognizable chemistry, but the peroxide, N-chloro amide/thioamide and unusual sulfur double-bond variants make part of the leading family chemically questionable as persistent drug-like molecules. The whole proposal set has median 26 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings. Compared with the parent, O-O single-bond proposals increase from 15 to 89 and N-halogen proposals from five to 27, so the new leading peroxide chemistry reflects a broader change in the sampled output.
liabilities: Diaryl O-O links and N-chloro or N-fluoro nitrogen sites introduce possible bond-cleavage and reactivity concerns; valid SMILES and objective values do not resolve those concerns.

The terminal sulfur-linked N-fluoro example and sulfur oxo/thioxo substitutions are chemically different from ordinary amides or sulfonamides and should not be interpreted as interchangeable polar linkers.
Nine proposals have at most three heavy atoms and four exceed 50, indicating occasional degeneration and overgrowth around an otherwise ring-rich population.
missing_features: The high-score neighborhood lacks demonstrated stable, conventional alternatives that retain the useful diaryl/polar arrangement while replacing its peroxide and N-halogen variants; the high-scoring ether shows such chemistry is already reachable.
Broader coverage of distinct compact aromatic carbonyl arrangements is less visible among the digest leaders than repeated changes around the same diaryl linker and thioamide family.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Replacing the diaryl ether link with an O-O link accompanies a score increase from 0.444319 to 0.455132 in a displayed local pair. Adding N-chlorination to the peroxide thioamide gives 0.439920, and the corresponding N-chloro carbonyl amide gives 0.438748. These observations show that the score tolerates the questionable bonds; they do not establish a benefit from N-chlorination or the chemical stability of a peroxide. Compact fused aromatic carbonyl structures also reach 0.436954 and 0.433013 without those particular bonds. At the low end, oxygen fluoride, methane and trifluoromethylamine score zero, while much larger, heavily elaborated molecules score about 1.05e-68 and 1.11e-62. The gradient therefore favors a structured intermediate-size aromatic/polar arrangement over both tiny fragments and overgrowth, while leaving some local chemical liabilities unpenalized.

per_task.generated_character: This is a large, highly aromatic, halogenated repertoire: median 35 heavy atoms, five rings, four aromatic rings and molecular mass 555.2495; the digest halogen rate is 0.8241. The highest molecule is a comparatively conventional three-ring aminoheteroaryl arylsulfonamide with methyl, fluoromethyl and aryl halogen substituents. Other leaders combine nitrogen/sulfur heteroaromatics with sulfonyl groups, carbonyls and heavily fused, iodine- or bromine-substituted ring systems. One displayed leader has eight rings and seven aromatic rings, and a terminal example contains selenium. The parent also contained large heteroaryl/sulfur frameworks and frequent peroxide or O-halogen connections. Current O-O single-bond proposals fall from 135 to five and O-halogen proposals from 93 to four, but substantial size and fusion remain: 146 current proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms.
liabilities: Large aromatic surfaces, iodine or bromine substitution and repeated ring fusion produce high molecular masses and little saturated shape in many leaders; no solubility or exposure measurements are supplied.

Some terminal molecules combine unusual nitrogen/oxygen/sulfur bonding or selenium heterocycles with already elaborate fused systems, increasing the uncertainty of interpreting them as ordinary medicinal chemistry.
The proposal distribution reaches 95 heavy atoms and 13 perceived rings; such overgrowth is not justified by the simpler structure at the highest displayed score.
missing_features: The output lacks consistent economical coverage of the productive aminoheteroaryl/sulfonamide arrangement: the highest displayed molecule is much simpler than several heavily fused alternatives.
Synthetic access and stable geometry are not established for the densely fused sulfur/nitrogen leaders; graph ring counts cannot substitute for chemically credible alternative ring systems.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The three-ring aminoheteroaryl sulfonamide scores 0.607553; a six-ring iodine-containing fused system scores 0.604646 and an eight-ring elaboration 0.598471. These examples do not support continually adding rings or heavy halogens as necessary for higher score. The low-scoring examples, around 0.265-0.292, also contain sulfones, carbonyls and sometimes several rings, but distribute them through more saturated or differently connected frameworks. Functional-group presence alone therefore fails to explain the gradient. A terminal small fluorinated diene scores 0.5 despite lacking the elaborate heteroaromatic architecture, so intermediate score itself is weak evidence of molecular completeness.

per_task.generated_character: The leading chemistry is substantially more conventional than the most unusual output elsewhere. The highest displayed molecule is a phenolic benzazepine-like structure: a seven-membered tertiary-amine ring fused to a benzene, with alkyl substituents, only 18 heavy atoms and molecular mass 247.382. A closely related leader has 17 heavy atoms. Another family is an arylpiperazine linked through a long alkyl chain to fluorinated naphthalene or aza-naphthalene rings; these examples have four rings and approximately 29-32 heavy atoms. The full set has median 26 heavy atoms and median sp3-carbon fraction 0.5. Parent leaders also included arylpiperazine chains and fused phenolic amines, but some were much more bridged or polycyclic; current median heavy-atom count falls from 30 to 26.
liabilities: Long alkyl chains in the arylpiperazine family increase conformational freedom, and extra halogenation increases mass, while the compact phenolic amine shows that neither feature is universally needed.
Some terminal structures add strained or partially dearomatized rings and duplicated arylpiperazine appendages; these are less straightforward chemical proposals than the leading conventional amines.
Thirty proposals contain an N-halogen bond, but the displayed highest-scoring conventional amines do not require that liability.
missing_features: No additional mandatory pharmacophoric group can be inferred from near-ceiling scores; the supported missing chemistry is configurationally specified coverage of the successful cyclic amines.

The compact leading phenolic amines have an unassigned stereogenic carbon. Across proposals, 562 molecules contain an unassigned centre and none has an assigned centre, leaving geometry-dependent interpretation unresolved.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Both the compact phenolic cyclic amine and the long-linker arylpiperazines reach scores above 0.999999. Their shared association is accessible tertiary-amine functionality presented with aromatic regions; extensive halogenation, multiple aromatic rings or one exact linker length is not required by all leading examples. An acetylated bis-sulfonamide aniline scores about 3.80e-05 and an aromatic carbamate about 9.56e-05, despite their heteroatoms and rings. The terminal shorter fluoroalkyl diazepane scores 0.036190, whereas related extended arylpiperazine architectures remain around 0.975-0.996. These observations indicate contextual amine/aromatic placement rather than generic nitrogen enrichment, and do not establish experimental receptor activity.

per_task.generated_character: The leading repertoire is dominated by fused azaaromatic systems with N-methylated cyclic amide carbonyls, supplemented by a bicyclic amine/ketone family carrying an N-ethoxy connection and an aromatic ether arm. The highest molecule has 30 heavy atoms, five rings and four aromatic rings; closely related N-alkyl variants occupy much of the digest.
